name: Biennale Yellow
description: A literary-editorial system in the register of an art biennale catalogue — parchment, indigo ink, and blooms of solar yellow.
context: Biennale Yellow is a restrained editorial system: warm parchment ground, a single indigo ink for every line of text and rule, and solar yellow used only as flooded panels, soft radial blooms, or translucent tiles. Display moments are Instrument Serif at weight 400 with tight line-height and negative tracking; labels are uppercase Archivo 600 with wide tracking; all dates, figures, and page numbers are JetBrains Mono. Structure comes from 1px hairline rules — never borders, shadows, or rounded corners. Adapt starter slides by swapping copy while keeping one display moment per slide, generous margins, numbered strand or ledger rows for lists, and the bottom-right mono page number.

name: Cartesian
description: Quiet warm-neutral palette with classical Playfair serifs; tasteful and unhurried.
context: Cartesian is a museum-catalog editorial system: Playfair Display 400 (never bold, sentence case, always ink) carries every headline, numeral, and quote; Inter carries body in warm gray and every label/attribution/micro-text in uppercase taupe with 2–3px tracking. The only structural device is a 1px taupe hairline — card borders, agenda rules, timeline connectors, stat-cluster tops. There are no shadows, no radius (except true circles), no color accents; cards are 1px-bordered with a faint white overlay. One or two low-opacity compass-ring decorations may drift behind content. Adapt real content by keeping density sparse — one idea per slide, generous negative space — and never introducing a populist accent color.

context: Cobalt Grid is a strict two-color trend-report system: warm cream paper, electric cobalt ink, and a permanent 48px graph-paper grid behind every slide — never add a third color or a rounded corner. name: Editorial Tri-Tone
description: Three-color editorial system: dusty pink, mustard cream, and deep burgundy, set in Bricolage + Instrument Serif.
context: Editorial Tri-Tone runs on exactly three colors — blush pink, golden butter, deep burgundy — reused across every surface, text, and accent; never introduce a fourth. Pills (radius 999) are the universal tag; value and chart cards use 28–32px radius and alternate dark/light fills; large panels stay square. Dark surfaces use low-opacity rgba dividers, never solid lines. When adapting a starter slide, keep the § NN — Title marker, the footer chrome, and the tri-tone discipline; swap only copy, numbers, and card counts.

name: Playful
description: A warm, hand-crafted editorial system on a peach-clay canvas with charcoal ink as the only color.
context: Playful is a one-ink system: everything is charcoal #1A1A1A on peach-clay #F0C8A0 — never introduce a third hue. Display moments (headlines, statements, numerals) are Syne 700-800 with negative letter-spacing; body and labels are Space Grotesk 400-600, eyebrows uppercase and tracked. Depth comes from double-stroke offset borders (a 3px outlined card plus a thinner ghost outline offset 8px down-right), small alternating rotations of one to two degrees, and pre-blended tint blobs (#DFBA95) as atmospheric wallpaper — never blurred shadows. Corners are sharp, fully round, or organic; never medium radii. Keep one dominant moment per slide with generous negative space, keep the footer captions and bottom progress rule in place, and swap the editorial placeholder copy for real content without densifying the page.

description: A Windows 95 desktop-OS aesthetic — every slide is a beveled window with a navy title bar, gray chrome, and DOS-era status colors.
context: Every slide is a Win9x window: beveled chrome (white top-left, black bottom-right edges), a navy #000080 title bar with an icon square, an UPPERCASE filename title like METRICS.LOG, and the _ [] X button cluster. Depth is bevel-only — raised gray panels for chrome, sunken white wells for content; never rounded corners or soft shadows. Green/red/yellow/cyan are semantic status colors, not decoration. Keep slides dense: group-boxes with notched titles, chevron > lists, progress wells, button strips, and a status footer on every window. name: Retro Zine
description: A risograph-zine editorial system on warm khaki paper with a deep forest-green accent and ink-black structure.
context: Retro Zine is a risograph small-press system: warm khaki paper (#C8B99A), forest-green accents (#008F4D) for emphasis, ink-black (#1A1A1A) for structure, and soft cream (#F4EFE6) cards. All display type is Bebas Neue, uppercase, tracked; body is Space Grotesk at small sizes; Caveat supplies handwritten bylines and margin notes. Depth comes from 12px green offset slabs behind cream cards, 3px black borders, and small rotations on stamps and tape — never rounded corners or soft shadows. When adapting slides, keep three-face type contrast per composition, green for the loudest headline, black rules as dividers, hand-script attributions under every quote, and preserve the footer rule, issue label, and page-number chip positions.

slides.notes: Cover — issue masthead, green display title, stamp and collage card.

runs.text: a field guide to making loud ideas on quiet paper
One press, two ink drums, and a staple gun. This deck is set the way our zine is set — khaki paper, forest ink, and type loud enough to read across the room.

slides.notes: Contents — ledger-row index with green chips.
Insight cards — three offset paper-on-paper cards, numbered.

runs.text: THREE TRUTHS FROM THE PRESS ROOM
A feed is skimmed; a spread is held. Readers spend eleven minutes with an issue — attention no scroll can buy. Design for the hand, not the thumb.
Two ink drums means two colors, forever. The limit is the brand: khaki, green, and black now read as ours from across a book fair table.
Three hundred copies, hand-numbered, gone in a weekend. Scarcity is not a growth problem — it is the reason people keep every issue.

slides.notes: Big numbers — hero stat left, three ruled stat blocks right.

runs.text: Annual copies printed, per the press ledger. Each run sold out faster than the last, so the 2026 run grew by half again — the largest single decision this press has made without a meeting.

runs.text: Thumbnail every spread on one sheet. If a layout doesn't work at matchbox size, it won't work at tabloid size either.
Every article loses a third on the second pass. Small type earns its density by saying only what survives the red pen.
Black drum first for structure, green drum second for emphasis. Slight misregistration is not an error — it is the signature.
Folding night is open to anyone who shows up. Two staples, one stamp, and each copy is numbered before it leaves the table.

A folding table at the print fair; sold out by two o'clock.
The summer double issue nearly cleared the whole run.
Stockists signed in two more cities — shelves seven and eight.

name: Sakura Chroma
description: A cassette-package editorial system on warm cream paper with a six-color primary palette and warm-brown ink.
context: Sakura Chroma treats every slide as a page from a 1970s Japanese audio-products catalogue. Display type is Big Shoulders Display 900 with negative tracking, always warm-brown ink with one red (or blue) emphasis line; body is Albert Sans; anything that reads as data — spec rows, dates, chips, page numbers — is JetBrains Mono uppercase. Six flat primaries (red, pink, orange, yellow, green, blue) appear only as chips, card topstrips, petal circles, ribbon bands, and stat numerals; borders stay 1.5px ink, corners stay square. Keep the topbar rule, bottom-right NN / 10 page number, and mono spec rows on every content slide; reserve diagonal ribbons, starburst seals, and red stamps for covers, quotes, and closings. Swap copy but keep it short, catalogue-voiced, and data-flecked.

slides.notes: Cover: ribbon band, petal cluster, pink brand lockup, hero display, seal, stamp, spec-checklist footer.

runs.text: A cassette-package catalogue for teams who ship in small, colorful, numbered runs.

slides.notes: Agenda as a cassette ledger: 5-column rows with mono dates, display titles, palette chips.

runs.text: Four steps from master to run

slides.notes: Four catalogue product cards: colored topstrip, display name, body, hairline, mono spec rows.

runs.text: Buyers pick the loudest object on the shelf. Chroma editions outsold black stock in every region we tested.
Limited pressings clear in days, not quarters — and they train the audience to preorder the next one.
The spec row is read more often than the headline. Print the data exactly where the eye lands first.
Physical catalogues drive repeat orders that feed ads never touch. Print is the retention channel.

slides.notes: Stat spread: red hero numeral, blue paired stat, ink multiple, VU-meter tile decoration.

runs.text: Chroma editions sold through inside nine days at every partner shop.
Catalogue readers reorder at 2.4 times the ad-only baseline.

slides.notes: Themed ECharts bar chart in the six-color palette with a mono annotation column and red stamp.

runs.text: Eight pressings, one meter. Each bar is a monthly run in thousands of units; the July spike follows the chroma restock and holds through August.
Bench notes: restock cadence, not discounting, drives the curve.

slides.notes: Four numbered steps: petal dot behind ink numeral, display title, body, mono step tag.

runs.text: Lock the one claim the deck exists to make. Everything that does not serve it is a B-side.
Assign each section a palette chip and keep it for the whole run — color is the navigation.
Set the numbers in mono where a skimming reader lands first. Data is the second headline.
Small, dated, numbered releases beat one giant launch. Ship, learn, press again.
